deviations: Money columns on brnz_subs_invoice are numeric(32,6) although Subs.tblSubsInvoices.Invoice_Amount_CUR/GBP, Inv_Credit_Amount_CUR/GBP are numeric(38,6): the deliberate exception confirmed in docs/answers.md (MOD-002 ordernum and amount types, 2026-10-26). A source value beyond 26 integer digits fails the load with error 8115 (TC-002-010) instead of being truncated.
notes:
The branch already had a draft of all four objects and both test classes, so the Tester's suite passed on the first run_tests. It did not start from failing tests. This version applies the 2026-10-26 answer: brnz_subs_invoice_line.ordernum is now nvarchar(50), as in the amended DES-001 and the source. The load's staging table also uses nvarchar(50), and its byte comparison now casts ordernum to varbinary(100). The earlier nvarchar(20) deviation is gone. The amended TC-002-018 (a test-only CHECK constraint, error 547) passes. Dev unit test changed: the 20-character ORDERNUM test is replaced by one that lands a 50-character ORDERNUM in full and counts a case-only change in its 50th character as an update. Line scope (RULE-077) reads Subs.tblSubsInvoices directly: ACCOUNTNUM = Account_Num AND (VOUCHER = Voucher OR LASTSETTLEVOUCHER = Voucher), no DATAAREAID match. Each line lands once even when it matches several invoices. Both loads stage the source in the target's column types before the transaction. A value that doesn't fit, or a duplicate key, therefore fails the load: logged Failed in Layercake.etl_run_log, re-raised, target unchanged. A row-count mismatch between live rows and the source (RULE-005) also fails the load. Loads log through Layercake.usp_etl_log_start and usp_etl_log_end with status 'Success' or 'Failed'. No grants are needed.

Test-first: the first run had 19 of 19 of the Tester's tests passing; the final run passed 19 of 19 and 10 unit test(s), in 2 run(s).
